ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$, with $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, and $CD\perp AB$ at $D$, if $AD=4$ and $BD=9$, what is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: $\because$ $\angle ACD + \angle BCD = \angle BCD + \angle B$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD = \angle B$,\\
Also, $\angle ADC = \angle BDC = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADC \sim \triangle BDC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{CD} = \frac{CD}{BD}$,\\
$\therefore$ $CD^2 = AD \cdot BD = 36$,\\
$\therefore$ $CD = \boxed{6}$ or $-6$ (discard).
